messages:
maya: Quick design call  do we ship a tiny persistent 'Get started' strip (corner pill) or an embedded demo-runner that appears inline when you land on Console? pros/cons?
chris: strip = predictable entrypoint, discoverable for new users. inline runner = faster path but can be missed. i'd pick strip for first-run. :+1:
anita: accessibility: persistent control easier to keyboard find. if we do inline, must add focusable anchors. also: any status badges need text labels, not color only.
devon: runner benefit: users can start a demo in-place with logs & quick feedback. but modal/inline must trap focus and announce start.
leo: mobile constraint: strip occupies corner space. compromise: icon-only collapsed on widths <=640px. expand on desktop.
maya: copy options for the strip label: "Get started", "Quickstart", "Starter". avoid "tour" language. preferences?
chris: "Get started" feels best. action oriented, low salesy vibe.
anita: keyboard shortcut idea: G then H to open helper. add discovery in command palette and aria-describedby on the opener.
devon: telemetry note: events: onboarding.strip.open, onboarding.runner.start, onboarding.checklist.complete. no sensitive payloads. opt-in for failure diagnostics.
ui-bot: Figma frames uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/zzz/getstarted-strip-vs-runner (preview).
maya: UX ordering: checklist vs samples. proposal: samples first (quick value) -> API key -> billing guard. anyone object?
chris: agree. samples first reduces early churn.
anita: a11y checklist I'll add to PR: SR announcements for open/close, live region for runner status, tab order, contrast checks (AA).
leo: engineering: preload just sample metadata (~40KB gz) so panel opens instantly. actual sample bundles load on run. feature-flag rollout 10% new accounts -> 100%.
devon: implementation detail: runner should open embedded with a small console area; provide "Open full workspace" as a follow-up CTA.
maya: UX polish: include a small "snooze" kebab (7/30/dismiss) so power users can mute the strip.
chris: metric goals: 30% sample-run within 7 days; reduce first-week support tickets re: getting started by 15%.
anita: final microcopy nits: keep labels short for localization, include tooltips for billing step (one-liner: "Set a billing guard to prevent unexpected charges").
maya: thanks allI'll turn this into a short spec + Figma diff and request design-review. tagging follow-up for next Tue.
